author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A new Gruffalo book has arrived for the first time in more than 20 years. “Gruffalo Granny,” released Thursday, reunites writer Julia Donaldson and illustrator Axel Scheffler for another story in the children’s series that began with “The Gruffalo.”

The book follows the Gruffalo and his daughter as they prepare for a visit from Granny. It extends a fictional world that has remained widely read even without frequent sequels. The series has sold more than 18.2 million copies, while the original book has been translated into 113 languages and dialects, according to Reuters.

Donaldson and Scheffler reflected on their long collaboration as they introduced the installment. Their combination of rhythmic storytelling and distinctive illustrations has carried the character from picture books into stage productions, screen adaptations and family attractions.

The creators did not announce another book, but they also left open the possibility of returning to the characters again. For now, “Gruffalo Granny” is the first expansion of the main story line in a generation, giving longtime readers a new chapter to share with children discovering the forest characters for the first time. The publication’s reception will show whether the series’ long gap has increased demand for further stories.
dek: Julia Donaldson and Axel Scheffler return with “Gruffalo Granny,” extending the children’s series after two decades without a new installment.
headline: First new Gruffalo story in more than 20 years reaches shelves
